sections.text: But that which clings blindly to one idea as if it were all, without logic, truth or insight, that has its origin in Darkness.
An obligatory action done by one who is disinterested, who neither likes nor dislikes it, and gives no thought to the consequences that follow, such an action is Pure.
यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहंकारेण वा पुनः।
But even though an action involve the most strenuous endeavour, yet if the doer is seeking to gratify his desires, and is filled with personal vanity, it may be assumed to originate in Passion.

So we had been discussing chapter 18, Moksha Sannyasa Yoga -- Yoga of Liberation through Renunciation. We had been discussing that this renunciation is of the actions which we are performing. Renouncing the actions will liberate me.
And then we have also seen that all actions cannot be renounced. Therefore, the actions which are helping me in purifying my internal instrument, the Antahkarana, those actions must be performed. And Bhagavan said, even for the wise people, even one who has achieved this knowledge -- if they stop performing these actions, there is the danger of getting pollution on their mind and intellect, or getting Tamas clouding over the mind and intellect again.
So they also continue these actions. Its like continuous maintenance. You have to continue to act in the manner which purifies our internal instrument, the Antahkarana.
Your actions should be for the purpose of purifying mind and intellect, so they remain in a Sattvic, clean mode where you can see the reality as it is all the time. And those actions must be performed in the right attitude and the right manner. Then we have also discussed that actions are prompted by knowledge -- I know something which I either like or dislike, and I come to the conclusion that thats the field of my action.
So knowledge is the propeller of action. The knowledge, the knower, and that which is to be known are the three propellers of action that propel you to act in this world. The last three verses analyzed knowledge, showing that even knowledge can be of three different types.
Like everything else we have discussed in Bhagavad Gita and Vedanta, things can be classified broadly into three categories: Sattvic, Rajasic, and Tamasic. Because these are the qualities of Maya. This world is nothing but the projection through Maya.
So everything in this world can be classified into these three categories. Knowledge can be Sattvic, Rajasic, or Tamasic. Sattvic knowledge is the one which makes me see the unity in diversity -- I can see the same immutable reality pulsating through all beings and things.
That knowledge which makes me see that is the Sattvic knowledge, the pure knowledge. The knowledge which makes me see the plurality -- that this world is made up of innumerable various things and beings unrelated to each other -- is called Rajasic, because it divides my world into I and the world. I am separate from this world. And this world is also not a one entity but conglomeration of various beings and things.
Thats Rajasic knowledge. And that creates again another division of the world: things which I like and things which I do not like. And then the third we have seen is Tamasic knowledge, which is a very narrow focus on a view or a philosophy.
One may say, this is reality. In Sanskrit we say kupamanduk, like the frog in a well. For that frog, the well is the world. There is nothing beyond that.
Obviously we know that is because of the frogs ignorance about the rest of the world. The same way, if we hold a view that this is real and everything else that other people tell me or believe is wrong, then its Tamasic knowledge. Its out of delusion, out of confusion, out of ignorance that I hold that view.
Thats Tamasic knowledge. Bhagavan said it is important for us to know what type of knowledge we have, because my actions will be guided by the views I hold because of my knowledge. We have seen the example that because I have a complete sattvic knowledge about my own self, when it comes to my body, the actions are completely synchronized.
That when there is a pain in our leg, my hand and arm rush there to help that. Thats because the knowledge is purely sattvic about myself that I pervade through this entire body. There is a unity in this diversity of limbs I have in my body.
And therefore my actions are also sattvic. There is no permission to be granted to the hand to go and massage the leg, which is if I have the similar reason for the rest of the world, my action will be exactly like that. So the next three verses say actions can also be classified -- depending on what propelled them -- into Sattvic, Rajasic, and Tamasic.
Niyatam Sangarahitam: that action which is done with the attitude that it needs to be done, and therefore Im doing it. My hand does not ask permission because it needs to be done. If I will have the same view, if theres any pain anywhere, I just wont be able to stop myself to go and help.
But right now I divide my world. Well, thats all happening in Egypt, so its not my problem. We are fine here. Let me call my brothers and sisters in India -- well, they are doing fine. So I think we are okay.
Because I dont feel that connection, that unity with the people who are suffering or people who need help. Bhagavan said, one who does this action -- the action which is ordained -- does it without attachment. There are no likes or dislikes.
There is no particular attachment in the left leg versus right leg. Even though my right leg is probably broken and needs more care. But I see them completely unattached manner.
My actions are ordained. In a sense, I feel compelled to act by my nature and my instinct because of the oneness I feel with that entity. Without any attachment, there is no particular reason that I want to help that person or want to do that action.
It just needs to be done. I dont have a particular love for that action or hate for their action. And there is no expectation of a particular result to come out.
Such an action is considered satwik. Thats because it will create the bliss internally for me in my internal instrument. Once I perform that action, there is no agitation.
There is no lingering thought, why did I do it? Was that the right thing to do or not? There is no after effect of my action and therefore it is sattvic. So there is a bliss inside. As Bhagavan said, the harmony outside the field in which Im acting, there is also no agitation.
Because I read something, the people Im working with, there is no agitation with them. They also feel harmony. And we know that when we are in some kind of community action where you really dont have anything to gain but just want to help out, you feel harmony there.
With other actions, you dont feel harmony. Thats because they fall into the next category -- Rajasic action. Most of our actions unfortunately fall into this category.
First of all, its done because its prompted by my desire. I want to get something out of it, therefore Im doing it. Their desire prompted action.
I want to gain something out of it. Why did you join this organization? Well, its good networking. Its a Rotary Club or a Lions Club or something.
Its supposed to be just for community development. But what does the marketing guy say? If you really want to be successful, you should join your local Rotary Club or a Lions Club or something. So you have a networking. By the way, some people may get benefit.
Thats a side effect of my joining. My main goal was to get a networking. I actually did a leadership metro course in 2003.
Its pretty prestigious -- a lot of CEOs and presidents and all that. Its basically for developing leadership in the area. But you ask them what the incentive is, and they say, Well, you will get to know all the CEOs and presidents in this town.
Good networking tool for your business. Now, by the way, if somebody is doing that and helping the community, it is still good enough. The people who are doing these actions for the wrong reasons but having a right effect on society -- let them do it, dont stop them. But it is not helping the person who is doing it.
So thats action which is prompted by desire. And again, it is also done with an ego. I am doing it, you know, nobody else was ready, but I said nobody else could have done it.
But I said I can do that. So kriyate Bahula Yasam and it requires lots of efforts. Something which does not come naturally to you obviously requires lots of effort.
The guy who is trained singer, when he sings, how much effort does he have to put nothing he naturally because hes trained. All his systems are wired for it. His vocal cords are trained for that.
And he just comes out and sings and goes away. Somebody like me, somebody says, Rajan, you have to perform on such and such. Well, I have to practice and make sure that I understand lots of effort because it does not come naturally to me.
So Bahula Yasam all our actions which are prompted by desire and done with ego require lots of efforts. And thats where we have a fatigue. When I say the burnout factor, you know, well, I had been helping this community for a long time.
Well, volunteers make sure they dont get burned out. If theyre truly volunteering, they will never get burned out. They get burned out because there was something other than just helping was involved.
Well, people are not giving me credit for what Im doing. That feeling makes you burn out of what you are doing. Bhagavan said they are doing it with lots of effort, and therefore there is fatigue, there is a burnout factor, there is disharmony and agitation within.
Sattvic action creates bliss within and harmony outside. Rajasic actions create agitation inside and disharmony outside. I wanted to do it, but he is now doing it. I wanted to be the president of this organization.
Even though I dont get anything out of it, nobody pays me for that -- but now he is doing it. So there is agitation, disharmony. Therefore these actions are called Rajasic. Good point that even the great political leaders, great social workers, and great leaders in the business world all fall into Rajasic action at the best of their behavior or the best of their intentions.
Because the same action can be Tamasic -- one which looks Rajasic but could be Tamasic. He says Rajasic actions are clearly better than Tamasic. You now just have to graduate from Rajasic to Sattvic to get the bliss which youre seeking, the happiness which you are looking for.
You have to transcend Rajasic into Sattvic. But be careful -- what you consider Rajasic may actually be Tamasic. So the next verse says what Tamasic action is: those actions are first of all prompted by delusion.
I want to do this because I do not know what is the right thing to do.

These verses classify actions themselves according to the three gunas. Sattvic action is niyatam (ordained/obligatory), performed sangam rahitam (without attachment), araga-dveshatah (without likes or dislikes), and aphala-prepsuna (without desire for results). Rajasic action is driven by desire (kamepsuna), performed with ego (sahamkarena), and involves bahula-ayasam (great effort/strain). The contrast is illuminating: sattvic action flows naturally and creates inner bliss and outer harmony, while rajasic action requires tremendous effort and creates internal agitation and external discord. The description of rajasic action in verse 24 deserves special attention. When work is desire-driven and ego-centered, it demands great effort. This explains burnout in volunteers and professionals alike - when we work for recognition, position, or personal gain, we become exhausted because we are fighting against the natural flow. Even great social workers and business leaders, at their best, often operate at the rajasic level. The challenge is to graduate from rajasic to sattvic action. Today, examine the effort level in your activities. Where does work feel like a struggle, requiring you to push through resistance? This may indicate rajasic motivation - desire for results or ego investment. Where does action feel effortless, almost doing itself? This points toward sattvic action. Choose one task that feels burdensome and ask: What am I really seeking from this? Can I perform it simply because it needs to be done, without attachment to how others receive it or what it produces? This shift from I want to this needs doing transforms the entire experience.
